skill.name: create-pr
skill.description: Guides pull request creation with Sentry conventions, including branch checks, change review, concise descriptions, title formats, reviewers, and issue links.
skill.summary: Create clear Sentry-style pull requests from committed branch changes.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline backticks in the skill instructions. The only confirmed issue is the PR creation example that uses shell command substitution for generated body text, which should be replaced with safer body handling.

remediation.issue: PR body text is passed through shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed temporary file or GitHub CLI body-file input instead of embedding generated body text in a heredoc command substitution.

remediation.issue: The skill can create and edit GitHub pull requests.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running gh pr create or gh pr edit commands that modify GitHub state.

content.value_statement: Writing clear PR descriptions can be slow and inconsistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Sentry-style pull request preparation.
actual_capabilities: Checks branch status and commit history before PR creation.
Reviews commit logs and diffs against main to understand scope.
Drafts concise PR descriptions using Sentry preferred structure.
Formats PR titles with feat, fix, or ref conventions.
Guides issue references and reviewer assignment when details are known.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI before creating or editing pull requests.
Assumes main is the comparison branch unless the user says otherwise.
Does not validate reviewer availability or team ownership.
Does not replace human review of branch state or PR scope.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Turn committed feature work into a clear PR title and concise description.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Requests
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Sentry review conventions before sending changes to reviewers.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Help an AI assistant inspect branch changes and produce a review-ready pull request.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, or Claude Code user

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small committed change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request description for my current branch. Follow the skill process and keep the body concise.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Bug Fix PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a branch fixes a tracked issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current branch against main and draft a Sentry-style bug fix PR. Include the issue reference I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review-Ready PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the branch has several commits or reviewers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the commits and diff on this branch. Propose a PR title, body, issue references, and one to three reviewers.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Complex PR Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for larger or risky changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a PR for this branch. Explain motivation, alternatives, review risks, and any areas reviewers should inspect carefully.

output_examples.input: A branch adds Slack thread replies for alert notifications.
output_examples.output: A concise PR body that explains the change, the motivation, the rejected alternative, and the related Sentry ticket.

output_examples.input: A branch fixes a null user API response.
output_examples.output: A bug fix PR description that states the failure mode, the fix, and the issue reference.

output_examples.input: A branch extracts duplicate validation logic into a shared module.
output_examples.output: A refactor PR description that states no behavior changed and explains why the shared module prepares future work.

best_practices: Commit all intended changes before asking the skill to create a PR.
Provide issue IDs, reviewer names, and special review concerns up front.
Confirm the final GitHub CLI command before it modifies remote state.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle unrelated features or fixes into one pull request.
Do not paste generated PR body text into shell commands without review.
Do not ask for broad reviewer lists when one to three reviewers are enough.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a process and command pattern. The user should confirm before running GitHub CLI commands.

faq.question: Which repository style does it follow?
faq.answer: It follows Sentry engineering practices for PR descriptions, title conventions, issue references, and reviewer selection.

faq.question: Does it include test plan sections?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly avoids test plan sections and checkbox lists in PR descriptions.

faq.question: Can it add reviewers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide GitHub CLI reviewer requests when usernames or team names are known.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Local git inspection does not need network access. GitHub CLI actions contact GitHub to create or edit pull requests.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Sentry?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is useful elsewhere, but Sentry naming and review conventions may need adjustment.
